name: Largest isosceles-free subset of the 100 by 100 grid
definition: Given a subset of the fixed zero-based integer grid {0,...,99}^2, maximize its cardinality subject to every three distinct selected points having three pairwise different squared side lengths. Collinear triples are included, so three equally spaced collinear points are forbidden.
constraints: each point is an integer pair (x,y) with 0 <= x,y < 100
for every three distinct points, all three squared Euclidean side lengths are pairwise different, including degenerate collinear triples
verification: Exact integer checks: for each selected apex, squared distances to every other selected point must be distinct. This rejects all isosceles triples, including collinear midpoint triples.

solution_format.points: list of distinct [x,y] integer pairs using zero-based coordinates

source_review.definition: Problem 6.59 of AlphaEvolve v3, fixed 100 × 100 integer grid, with collinear midpoint triples included. The published 1-based problem is translation-equivalent to the notebook’s 0-based coordinates. Maximize cardinality.
source_review.sources: The paper reports 164 for n=100 and explicitly states that the authors believe it is not optimal. The official notebook at 8f447457957deac61e28bf1676746f0753b3b2f8 supplies its 164 zero-based coordinates. PatternBoost reports 160 as an AI-assisted earlier lower bound.
source_review.human_baseline: The four-digit ternary set with digits 0 and 1 has no three-term arithmetic progression. Embedding it in one grid row gives 16 points. This exact frozen comparison is a weak human-method baseline.
source_review.independent_check: Sorted all squared distances in an independent integer matrix. Verified 2 initial points, 112 from seeded greedy search, 16 from the human method and 164 from the public witness. Strict replay, forged scores, duplicates and execution failures were checked.
